content:
I have to admit, my DIY iPhone camera mod does look a little ridiculous — but it's actually made shooting photos and videos on the iPhone far more practical and enjoyable.

Originally, the modification was made to solve a specific filming scenario, but I didn't expect that in the end I would keep reaching for it again and again…

In the world of compact cameras, one of the longest-running debates is whether you need a viewfinder. Enthusiasts have long favoured electronic viewfinders (EVF) over optical ones, but EVFs have now become so good that virtually nobody cares about the difference between the two anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder does offer one very practical advantage over using the rear screen for framing — especially under harsh sunlight. Even with the screen brightness turned up to maximum, when the sun is strong it can still be very difficult to see what you're actually shooting, and you may also have to contend with screen glare.

Although in London this hasn't traditionally been much of an issue, this summer has seen record-breaking heatwaves, and honestly, I think the last time I saw rain here was about thirty years ago.

But for me, the significance goes beyond that. I feel there's a psychological difference between simply seeing what's inside the frame and being able to see the surrounding environment at the same time while shooting. Sometimes it's precisely that feeling that makes me prefer using a dedicated camera over a phone.

When I was choosing a camcorder a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was clearly a hugely popular choice, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end, I decided it wasn't a major issue for me, because most of the time I was shooting indoors, and when I was out and about, adding a large screen with a sun hood solved most of the problems.

But sometimes I wanted something more portable than a full external monitor setup, so I found a simple accessory for outdoor use. It's a combination of a sun hood and a magnifier that attaches magnetically to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I was about to have a shoot that required using both the BMPCC 4K and an iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test on set and found that this viewfinder accessory was genuinely excellent. Since the screen size of the BMPCC 4K is very similar to the iPhone, I wondered whether it could be used on the iPhone as well.

Of course, the iPhone doesn't have a magnetic mounting system, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it against the magnifier by hand works perfectly fine. The results blew me away, especially when using the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've used this accessory in quite a few shooting situations. Being able to see the screen more clearly under harsh sunlight, combined with that sense of immersion, makes the whole experience much more enjoyable. My iPhone has always been my main camera, and with this DIY modification, I think there'll be more situations where just taking my phone out is enough.

Is this design ridiculous or genius? Let me know your thoughts in the comments. If you think it's the latter, then I'm sorry to report that the product I bought appears to have been discontinued, and I've never seen a similar design made for screens larger than three inches. If you find one, please drop a link in the comments.
